It's been a tough year, doctor. For the past twelve months, it feels like I've been wading through thick mud. There’s this continuous, heavy sadness that just sits on me, and nothing brings me joy anymore. My husband tries, but even things I used to love, like our weekend hikes or even just reading a good book, feel utterly bland. My mind just tires out so quickly; trying to focus on my bioinformatics work feels like pushing a boulder uphill. Sometimes, honestly, I just think, "I wish I wasn't here," or "I just want it all to end," though I'd never act on it.

Then, about a month ago, things shifted. It was like someone flipped a switch. I found myself buzzing with energy, barely needing an hour or two of sleep, and waking up feeling completely refreshed. My thoughts would just race, and I’d talk so fast, stringing ideas together, sometimes even my husband couldn’t keep up. I’d be constantly doing something – pacing while on a call, fidgeting, unable to just sit and relax. My mood was all over the place too; one minute I’d be on top of the world, feeling brilliant and creative, then frustrated and snappy if something didn’t go my way. It didn't really mess up my job, though, I was actually getting a lot done. But now, that rush is fading, and I can feel the darkness creeping back in.

A. Anorexia Nervosa
    B. Bipolar I Disorder
    C. Bipolar II Disorder
    D. Persistent Depressive Disorder
